title: fix(lint): one-line verdicts for the sort, search, form-predicate, bulk-dispatch, component-type and preset-comparand rules; `os explain RULE_ID` carries their reasoning
body:
Part of #22161
Clause-②: no

Stage 2 of the card, slice 6: the 12 rule ids of six whole `packages/lint` source files — the list-view sort and search rules, the metadata-form predicate-path rule, the bulk-dispatch contract rule, the component-type rule and the preset-comparand rule. The card stays open for the later slices listed under "Remaining for later slices" below.

## What changes

- **One verdict line per finding.** Each finding of the 12 ids prints a `message` of one verdict sentence. Every finding the rules' own suites fire is now 193 characters or fewer, and the runtime publish gate's suites (the whole `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` suite) 137 or fewer; the longest of each id was 287 to 927 before.
- **The verdict no longer repeats what `where` names:** the view that wires an action (`action-dispatch-contract-mismatch`'s `where` is `view "task" · list · bulkActions`). This follows slice 4's accepted design call.
- **Two shared clauses, one wording each:**
  - the unprovisioned-anchor ids (`sort-field-unprovisioned`, `searchable-field-unprovisioned`) print the same one-clause cause the converted anchor rules already print, `unprovisionedAnchorVerdict()` from `system-fields.ts` (slice 2's short form);
  - the two virtual-entry ids (`sort-field-unsortable`, the virtual arm of `searchable-field-unsearchable`) state the storage fact through one new clause, `virtualFieldClause()`, exported from `validate-searchable-fields.ts` (not on the barrel; the sort file already imports from it).
- **A quoted text is quoted to its verdict, never rewritten:**
  - a retired component type (`user:profile`, `element:filter`, `element:form`, `ai:chat_window`) is quoted to the HEAD of its `RETIRED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES` prescription — the clause before its first dash, else its first sentence (`retiredTypeHead()`, exported, not on the barrel) — and the verdict says the parse refuses the node by name and that `os validate` prints the whole prescription. The rule still authors no second copy: the test holds that the head is a prefix of the map's text, where it used to hold byte equality.
  - `filter-preset-comparand` opens with the first sentence of the refusal the schema door shares (`bareDateRangePresetComparandMessage`, cut at its first period: `"last_30_days" is a dashboard date-range PRESET name, not a filter value`), then the operator and the preset's `{date-macro}` window (`presetComparandVerdict()`, exported, not on the barrel). The window is read from `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS` in the refusal's own spelling, and a test holds the two equal for all 13 presets; another holds every preset under the longest operator spelling (`greater_than_or_equal`) to the 200 bound.
  - `searchable-field-unsearchable` quotes at most three names of an object's declared set, then `(and N more)` (`declaredRoster()`); the `fix:` line still names `OBJECT.searchableFields`.
- **The reasoning moves to `RULE_EXPLANATIONS`** (`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`), 12 new entries, so `os explain RULE_ID` prints it and the CLI's `rule:` line ends with the pointer for these ids. No CLI source changes: `explainPointer()` and `os explain` resolve any key the table holds (`packages/cli/test/explain-rule-id.test.ts` iterates every key; run below); `node bin/run-dev.js explain sort-field-unknown` prints the entry. The 75 entries already in the table are byte-equal at the head; the one existing constant this slice reuses, `UNPROVISIONED_ANCHOR_CAUSE`, changes only its `//` doc comment (it now names the two new ids it serves).
- **Nothing else moves.** Rule ids, severities, `path`, `hint` (the `fix:` line) and what each rule accepts or refuses are unchanged. No condition, branch, dedupe key or skip moved; every hunk in the six rule files is a `message` expression, a comment, an import, a verdict helper, or the removal of a value that only fed the old message. The helper and plumbing hunks, each message-only:
  - `validate-action-dispatch-contract.ts`: `check()` loses its `viewLabel` parameter, which fed only the message (the two call sites drop the argument; `where` still carries the label); `CONTRACT_PROSE` (record of strings) becomes `DELIVERS` (record of strings) and `MISFIRE`'s two strings are shortened. `collectDeclaredContracts`, the `declared === wired` early return and both skips are untouched.
  - `validate-searchable-fields.ts`: the auto-default arm's `why` for a system/audit column loses its trailing clause (`'a system/audit column, which the auto-default set never includes'` → `'a system/audit column'`); its three-way choice and the `continue` on an unreadable type are unchanged. The `SEARCHABLE_TEXTUAL_TYPES` / `SEARCHABLE_ENUM_TYPES` imports, which fed only the old message, go (the explanation writes the list out; the rule's test holds it equal to the two constants).
  - `validate-sortable-fields.ts` and `validate-searchable-fields.ts`: `unprovisionedAnchorCause` → `unprovisionedAnchorVerdict` (string → string).
  - `validate-predicate-path-refs.ts`: a `FAILS_OPEN` constant, the consequence clause both resolution verdicts end with.
  - No helper changed shape (no string → boolean); no truth table is involved.
- `.changeset/22161-lint-slice-6-one-line.md`: `@objectstack/lint` `patch`, naming every door that prints the new text (below). `Clause-②: no` follows the contract review on slice 1 (its section ②): `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` entries are data in an existing export.
- **One docs transcript follows the text:** `content/docs/data-modeling/schema-design.mdx` quoted `searchable-field-unknown`'s old message as what `os validate` prints for a dotted entry; its two message lines now read the new verdict (the quoted `hint:` is unchanged). This file is outside the claim's file surface; see "Acceptance notes".
- **Rider:** one text-only assertion in `packages/lint/src/validate-react-page-props.test.ts` (the react page's ListView `searchableFields` prop runs the shared searchable core); no `packages/cli/test` or `packages/metadata-protocol` file asserts these ids' message text (the consumers pin rule ids and `path`), so neither is touched.

The verdict forms, the longest of each id as the suites fired them (census below):

```text
list-view sort orders by "nope", which is not a field on object "showcase_ext_customer", so every load of this view answers 400 INVALID_SORT. Did you mean "name"?
list-view sort orders by "expected_revenue" on object "crm_opportunity", a virtual 'formula' field: its value is computed on read and never stored, so there is no column to ORDER BY
list-view sort: 'organization_id' is an injected column with no storage on external object 'showcase_ext_customer', so its ORDER BY is dropped and every fetch returns rows in an arbitrary order
list-view searchableFields entry "email" is not a field on object "crm_account", so the engine drops it from the search. Did you mean "billing_email"?
list-view searchableFields entry "account_id" is of type 'lookup', which 'search' cannot scan, so the auto-default search set excludes it and list search answers 400 INVALID_FIELD
list-view searchableFields entry "status" is outside the declared searchableFields (subject, case_number, description), so list search answers 400 INVALID_FIELD
searchableFields: 'owner_id' is an injected column with no storage on external object 'ext_customer', so 'search' never matches it and the searchable set is narrower than it declares
predicate references `data.__no_such_key__`, but `__no_such_key__` is not a key of `data`, so the predicate never evaluates and the console fails open: the element always renders
predicate names `type` bare, but it is a key of the edited schema with its `data.` root dropped, so the predicate never evaluates and the console fails open: the element always renders
predicate compares against `record.active` on the RIGHT of `==`, which this form reads as the literal string "record.active", so the result never depends on that path's value
predicate compares against the unquoted word `active` on the RIGHT of `==`, which reads as a literal today but is outside the declared subset and breaks under the real CEL evaluator
action "recalc_selection" declares execution: 'aggregate', wired as execution: 'perRecord' (one call per row: `recordId`, no `_selectedIds`), so its body takes its single-record branch
`record:approval_decison` is not a declared type of the reserved `record:` namespace, so the page draws a placeholder in its place. Did you mean 'record:approval_decision'?
`element:filter` was removed in @objectstack/spec 17 (ADR-0049), so the parse refuses this node by name (`os validate` prints the prescription)
"last_quarter" is a dashboard date-range PRESET name, not a filter value as a bare "nin" comparand; its window is { $between: ['{last_quarter_start}', '{last_quarter_end}'] }
```

## Shared prose: written once (the dispatch's mechanism assumption 2)

| shared sentence | ids | verdict clause (rule files) | explanation (`rule-explanations.ts`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| what an unprovisioned anchor is | `sort-field-unprovisioned`, `searchable-field-unprovisioned` (and slices 2 and 5's two anchor ids) | `unprovisionedAnchorVerdict()` (`system-fields.ts`, existing) | `UNPROVISIONED_ANCHOR_CAUSE` (existing, text byte-equal) |
| a formula field has no stored column | `sort-field-unsortable`, `searchable-field-unsearchable` (virtual arm) | `virtualFieldClause()` (new) | `VIRTUAL_FIELD_STORAGE` |
| what the list-view field rules do not judge | the three sort ids, `searchable-field-unknown` | — | `LIST_VIEW_FIELD_SKIPS` |
| a list view's narrowing becomes the `$searchFields` override | `searchable-field-unknown`, `searchable-field-unsearchable` (`searchable-field-unprovisioned` states its own consequence) | — | `SEARCH_FIELDS_ECHO` |
| a dead predicate fails open | `predicate-path-unresolved`, `predicate-path-unrooted` | `FAILS_OPEN` | `PREDICATE_FAIL_OPEN` |
| which form predicates are judged, against which schema | `predicate-path-unresolved`, `predicate-path-unrooted` | — | `PREDICATE_FORM_SCOPE` |
| a preset name's refusal | `filter-preset-comparand` and the schema door in `@objectstack/spec` | `presetComparandVerdict()` cuts the shared refusal's first sentence | — (the explanation states the rest once) |
| a retired type's prescription | `component-type-unknown` and the parse door | `retiredTypeHead()` cuts the map's entry | — (the explanation names where the whole prescription prints, and restates none; a test holds that) |

The explanation module imports nothing, so the facts it writes out are held to their sources by the rules' tests: the auto-default type list to `SEARCHABLE_TEXTUAL_TYPES` + `SEARCHABLE_ENUM_TYPES`, the virtual-type claim (`formula` alone) to `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`.

## Census (taken first, before any edit, at the base `61bea24207`)

Method: slice 4's scratch preload (`NODE_OPTIONS=--import`, never committed), which patches `Array.prototype.push` to record every finding-shaped object (`rule` + `message`) of the 12 ids, deduped by (rule, message), with its push site, in every vitest worker. Lengths are `message` alone; the printed line adds `where` and `: `. Rows from `os lint`'s own printer (`commands/lint.ts`) are excluded.

- **`packages/lint` suite** at the base: 135 files, 6,264 passed (the CLI closure build put the `dist/` its dist-reading tests wait for in place). **All 12 ids fired, every one over 200**, from 25 push sites; the longest of each matches the claim's figures exactly.
- **`packages/cli` unit tier**, the whole project (279 files) against the base's lint dist: 277 files and 4,097 tests passed; the two that did not load (`published-subpath-console.pin`, `published-subpath-hook-body.pin`) need `packages/cli/dist`, which was not built then (they refuse before running, naming the build). **It fires none of the 12 ids.** Positive control, same preload: `field-no-consumers` added to the recorded set is recorded (64 characters). The integration tier is declared to CI: no file in it names these ids, and its fixture shapes (`visibleWhen` on object fields, a `record.*` scope) are not ones these rules judge.
- **Runtime publish gate:** the whole `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` suite (224 files, 221 run, 28,047 passed), which reads `@objectstack/lint` from its built `dist/`. The before run read a lint `dist/` built from the base, on a clean tree (the closure build above, before the first edit); the after run read the dist rebuilt at the slice's commit (marker: `so the engine drops it from the search` 1 hit each in `dist/index.js`, `index.cjs`, `runtime.js`, `runtime.cjs`; the old `The declaration is stale: searching it can never match` 0). It fires two ids, from a flattened list overlay's `sort` (`runtime-authoring-gate.public-form-intake.test.ts`) and an object's `searchableFields` (`protocol-publish-drafts-object-field-refs.test.ts`); both suites pin the rule id and `path`, never the text.
- Not measured: the example apps (outside the dispatch's list; slice 5 measured them for its own ids).

| rule id | lint suite before: messages · longest | lint suite after: messages · range | runtime-gate suite before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sort-field-unknown` | 8 · 287 | 8 · 129–162 | 262 → 137 |
| `sort-field-unsortable` | 6 · 369 | 6 · 161–181 | — |
| `sort-field-unprovisioned` | 6 · 844 | 6 · 183–193 | — |
| `searchable-field-unknown` | 14 · 295 | 14 · 108–150 | 256 → 111 |
| `searchable-field-unsearchable` | 12 · 449 | 12 · 137–179 | — |
| `searchable-field-unprovisioned` | 3 · 512 | 3 · 171–182 | — |
| `predicate-path-unresolved` | 6 · 371 | 6 · 156–178 | — |
| `predicate-path-unrooted` | 1 · 434 | 1 · 184 | — |
| `predicate-rhs-path-shaped` | 12 · 648 | 12 · 160–181 | — |
| `action-dispatch-contract-mismatch` | 5 · 927 | 3 · 174–184 | — |
| `component-type-unknown` | 16 · 807 | 16 · 120–172 | — |
| `filter-preset-comparand` | 43 · 669 | 43 · 136–174 | — |

All 25 push sites fire before and after. One lint test reads the package's `dist/` and fires `filter-preset-comparand` through it; the after run was taken on the rebuilt dist, so it reports the new text too (a first after run on the base dist recorded that one old message, and was discarded). `action-dispatch-contract-mismatch` loses two distinct messages because the old message echoed the view label, which is the finding's `where`.

## Doors that print the new text

Read from the registry (`authoring-rules.ts`: every entry is `commands: ALL`; `validatePresetComparands` is `CLI_AND_RUNTIME` with `runtimeTypes: ['dashboard', 'view', 'object', 'page', 'flow', 'report']`, `validatePredicatePathRefs` with `['view']`, `validateComponentTypes` is `CLI_ONLY`; the reference-integrity suite, `CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, dispatches `validateSearchableFields` on `['flow', 'view', 'object']`, `validateSortableFields` on `['flow', 'view']` and `validateActionDispatchContract` on the default `['flow']`) and the CLI's callers (`commands/validate.ts`, `compile.ts`, `lint.ts`, `verify.ts`, `utils/scaffold-validate.ts`, which `init.ts` and `generate.ts` run):

| door | ids | what changes |
|---|---|---|
| `os validate`, `os build` (and `os compile`, which `os dev` runs per compile), `os lint`, `os verify`, the `os init` / `os generate` scaffold check | all 12 | the text-face verdict line; the `rule:` line gains the `os explain` pointer; `os validate --json` `errors` and `os build --json` author-time `issues` carry the new `message` |
| runtime publish gate (Studio, REST `/meta`, MCP) | the three `searchable-field-*` ids on a `view`, `object` or `flow` write; the three `sort-field-*` ids on a `view` or `flow` write; the three `predicate-*` ids on a `view` write; `filter-preset-comparand` on a `dashboard`, `view`, `object`, `page`, `flow` or `report` write | the 422 issue `message` and the `OS_ALLOW_UNLINTED_METADATA_WRITES` refusal log line |
| never at the runtime gate | `component-type-unknown` (CLI only); `action-dispatch-contract-mismatch` (it runs there only on a `flow` write, whose snapshot carries no actions, so its declaration map is empty and it returns before judging) | |
| unchanged | every `hint`; every other rule id | |

Every row is named in the changeset.

## Tests

The rule suites import the rule source; the CLI and runtime-gate suites read the rebuilt `@objectstack/lint` dist.

- **Each rule's own suite pins the new shape**, as in slices 2–5. All six test files wrap their rule import (and `checkSortDeclaration` / `checkSearchableFieldList`, the exported cores) and record every finding their cases fire; a final case in each holds every recorded verdict of its ids to one line of at most 200 characters, behind a coverage control (each id fired; for `component-type-unknown`, the retired arm fired for every retired type). A second block per file pins, per id, that `explainRule(id)` exists and still names what the verdict stopped saying, and holds the explanation's written-out lists to their spec sources. New exact pins: the sort virtual verdict, the two predicate resolution verdicts (one consequence clause), both dispatch directions, the namespace verdict, the preset verdict for an injected `created_at`; `retiredTypeHead` has its own cases (dash, first sentence, never rewrites). Every refusal assertion, rule id, severity, `path`, `where` and hint pin is unchanged. The measured-consequence pins that read the old text (ADR-0015 in the anchor messages, the skill-parity full-message pins of the searchable verdicts, the preset refusal's full text) moved to the new text or to the explanation.
- **Lint suite:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` at `8ad8e8bdf4` (lint source byte-identical to the head `cd82744e3f`, which changes only the changeset): Test Files 135 passed (135), Tests 6,295 passed (6,295); lock VERDICT command-exit 0 (31 new cases).
- **Lint build + typecheck:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run typecheck`: VERDICT command-exit 0; `check:test-typecheck` OK, 2 files, 6 errors and 2 pinned signatures held (the test layer compiles under `tsconfig.test.json`, so the six test files are covered).
- **CLI**, against the rebuilt lint dist: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 test/explain-rule-id.test.ts test/commands.test.ts test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts test/migrate-meta-engine-guidance.test.ts`: Test Files 4 passed (4), Tests 91 passed (91). `explain-rule-id.test.ts` iterates every `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` key, so all 12 new ids resolve through `os explain`, `explainPointer` and the listing. `migrate-meta-engine-guidance.test.ts` is the tracker-id refusal (mechanism assumption 4).
- **Runtime gate:** the whole `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` suite, before and after (census above): Test Files 221 passed | 3 skipped (224), Tests 28,047 passed | 19 skipped, both runs; lock VERDICT command-exit 0.
- **Spec `repo` project (mechanism assumption 3):** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project repo --maxWorkers=2` (= `test:repo`): Test Files 55 passed (55), Tests 971 passed (971); lock VERDICT command-exit 0, at `8ad8e8bdf4`. Two of its tests walk `packages/lint/src` as a corpus: `src/shared/retired-key-migrate-sentence.test.ts` (the `os migrate meta` sentence scanner; the new text carries no such sentence, grep 0) and `src/identity/position-delegatable-enforcer.pin.test.ts` (exported `security-*` rule id constants; this slice declares none). The other `lint/src` mentions under `packages/spec/src` name `validate-component-props.test.ts` in path lists or are comments.
- **Tracker ids (mechanism assumption 4):** no `#` plus digits in any printed message (0 in the census's 142 after messages) or explanation (`rule-explanations.test.ts` refuses one in every paragraph); the citations stay in `//` comments and test names.
- **Ablation** (one-shot, from the committed state `8ad8e8bdf4`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` wrap mode under the verify lock, plus a shell `trap` restoring `HEAD`). The rule suites import the rule source, so there is no dist leg. `sort-field-unknown`'s pre-slice message was restored verbatim (the mutated block checked equal to the base file's) through the anchor of its new message: anchor x1 to x0, blob `ace03ff2b4d3` to `8373465e586c`. Predicted before the run: exactly the bound pin goes red, since the old text still carries every fragment the other cases pin (`Did you mean "amount"?`, `400 INVALID_SORT`). Observed: `src/validate-sortable-fields.test.ts` gave Test Files 1 failed (1), Tests 1 failed | 45 passed (46); the one red case was "every verdict the cases above fired is one line of at most 200 characters" (269 characters). Restored: blob after restore `ace03ff2b4d3` == blob at HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty.
- **ESLint, narrowed:** `npx eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 14 changed `.ts` files gave 14 files in the report, 0 errors, 0 warnings. `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules), so no untouched file's verdict can move. A control-character scan of every changed file found no match.
- **Gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` with no paths, on the head `cd82744e3f` (merge base `61bea24207`; the derived set is identical to the one at `8ad8e8bdf4`), derived 90 commands. I ran 88 of them sequentially, each with its own log and its exit code captured before any pipe: all 88 exited 0. Two are NOT MEASURED, as the dispatch directs: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (it needs the whole-workspace build), and `pnpm check:type-check-debt`, which is `check-type-check-coverage.mjs --re-measure` in `package.json` (it builds every package); its non-re-measuring half is the same command as `check:type-check-coverage`, which ran and exited 0. `--ran` gave `Run reconciliation — 90 derived, 88 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 2 UNRUN` (those two). I also ran the 51-family "Artifact rosters" block the same run prints, 47 of them (one, `check:engine-double-contract`, is also a derived command): all exited 0 (14 of the 51 are checker-health `--self-test` rows, which grade a checker and not this diff; four keep their roster in a directory this diff touches — `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity` — all green). The three PR-context guards (`check-closing-target-claim`, `check-partof-closing-keyword`, `check-single-claim-paths`) need this PR's number and body, so they run against this PR after it opens; their readings are in the report on the card. On a first pass at `8ad8e8bdf4` (the same 135 commands, all 0 at the second pass), `check:skill-examples` and `check:published-readme-exports` refused with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3, nothing measured: seven packages' `dist/*.d.ts` absent); I built exactly those seven (`client-react`, `cli`, `organizations`, `service-knowledge`, `knowledge-memory`, `knowledge-ragflow`, `embedder-openai`; lock VERDICT 0, 48s) and both exited 0. The long ones on the shared box: `check:query-options-erasure` 267s, `check:slot-lookup` 135s, `check-comment-mask-corpus` 103s.

## Acceptance notes

- **One more `fix:` line now points at text the verdict quotes only in part:** `component-type-unknown`'s retired arm ends its hint "Apply the prescription above", and the verdict now quotes the prescription's head and says `os validate` prints the whole of it (`os validate` and `os build` refuse the same name at the parse with the whole prescription; `os lint`, which does not parse, prints the head).
